comments.author: @yelenayakovleva7901
comments.text: Great podcast. :) You know what I found interesting? AI, simply speaking, is a product of companies, let say it is a sophisticated tool as a product. It is incorporated into internet, being a product and a part of internet at the same time. Now, we have a product producing the product, which is making money from the end users. Simply put, we have a pencil charging human money if human wanted to use it, even if human created the pencil for the use by human. I found it a bit awkward in a way, that if before we were at state when we were using tools for our productivity, now tools using us for their productivity to produce more products which are going to use us for their productivity. I mean, everything is crumbled right now, in some weird state of undefined meanings. The burden of paying money is still on the end users of products which are using humans for their productivity. I think, there is something wrong in math economically. I think if to look at it in a big picture then end users are losing by paying for the product produced by a product. It is kind of double taxes. Am I missing something maybe here? :) Unless, YouTube has a policy that channels produced by AI could not be monetized. Is there such a thing? Human productivity could not compete with productivity done by industrial tech. So far, all tech was as an extension of our human abilities. If need speed, we have a car as a product, if we need clothing, we have machines producing it, but not car, or clothing able to produce the product of their own. Now with AI being a sophisticated product we have the product which is producing a product. If, for example, watching your channel, I know that you as a human creator spent your energy and time into producing this video, and simply watching it, likening it, subscribing to your channel, I, as a human, participating in a transactional microprocess for you to build up income for all your efforts put into producing this video. You then distributing your earned income further in economy, applying your part into your own transactional processes, distributing your earned part between other humans who are going to provide you with your necessities. So, in this kind of process economy is working. When it is coming to AI, then what? Where is the further distribution into economy whatever earnings AI made by being a sophisticated product producing a product? So, big, fat tech companies should start to think about it along with big, fat government, before economy is going to be either reject AI as a part of daily life of human society, or just simply collapse with AI together. Either one, it would be unfortunate outcome if not regulated wisely. Imho.

comments.author: @InferiorI
comments.text:
My channel has never been anything other than AI gen content. I spend as much time making a short video as anyone who is not using AI tools. I do a lot of editing, inputting my human direction. I do it because I like it.

I've met some really talented, established, content creators producing with AI. I don't count myself as one. I'm slowly acquiring subscriptions to the tools, one by one.


The dead net theory manifesting is a sad thing. AI is not the problem. People are the problem. 

Using AI is a fraction of previous production costs, but it is not cheap. Not for anyone outside of business use. Business throws money at AI for a return. Standard practice.

There has always been a lot of hype. Model demo's are great. Polished content from big budgets are great. Reality is no single model to date generates every component of a production, not to professional level. It's an expensive business to access everything needed.

Automated content seems to be good business. I'd be happy to see people reject it. I'm not sure though, that audiences can differentiate business from creative endeavor.
